title: Spudlight / Starchforce — Plant Carbon Storage Benchmark
status: archive-generated biological benchmark instantiating the existing storage/release model; not a new force
abstract: This benchmark gives the existing Spudlight/Starchforce storage-release formalism one concrete scientific domain: plant carbon and tuber starch storage. It treats the model as an ordinary stock-flow system rather than a fundamental force. The state K(t) is a measurable starch or declared carbohydrate pool, input J_in(t) is a measured or inferred storage flux, eta controls mobilization/release, and Gamma represents other turnover or loss. The scientific test is whether the linear storage-release model predicts held-out stock trajectories better than simpler persistence or unconstrained stock-flow baselines, and whether a saturating release term earns its extra complexity.
research_question: Can a minimal storage-release model predict measured plant/tuber carbon or starch dynamics with identifiable parameters and outperform simpler baselines on held-out observations?

provenance.historical_project_vocabulary: Spudlight and Starchforce are project terms with symbolic and theological meanings.
provenance.scientific_descendant_authorship: The plant-carbon benchmark is a later archive-generated biological instantiation of an ordinary stock-flow model, not evidence for a fifth force or Tim-authored plant-physiology law.

state_and_units.K: starch mass, carbon-equivalent stock or another explicitly declared storage proxy; use one unit consistently, e.g. g starch or g C
state_and_units.J_in: storage input flux in stock-units per time
state_and_units.J_out: mobilization/release flux in stock-units per time
state_and_units.t: time in a declared unit such as hours or days

equations.linear_balance: dK/dt = J_in(t) - eta K - Gamma K

initial_condition.default: K(0) is either directly measured at the first observation or estimated as a parameter with uncertainty.
initial_condition.rule: Do not silently choose K(0) to improve fit; its treatment must be declared before model comparison.

measurement_model.direct_stock: If laboratory starch/carbon stock is measured directly, h(K)=K after unit conversion and calibration.
measurement_model.proxy: If K is inferred from a proxy, h must state the calibration relation and uncertainty rather than treating proxy units as stock units.
measurement_model.error: epsilon_i represents measurement uncertainty; process discrepancy should be modeled separately if required.

baseline_hierarchy.model: dK/dt=J_in(t)-J_out(t) with J_out observed or independently prescribed
baseline_hierarchy.role: tests whether fitted first-order release is actually needed
higher-complexity candidate admitted only if data justify it

identifiability.warning: With stock observations alone, eta and Gamma can be difficult or impossible to separate because only eta+Gamma may control the linear decay timescale.
identifiability.repair: Measure release/respiration/turnover channels independently where possible, fix one rate from external measurements with provenance, or report only identifiable combinations.
identifiability.saturating_warning: J_max and K_half can be strongly correlated unless observations span a wide enough range of K.

calibration_protocol: Freeze the biological system, stock definition, units and sampling interval.
Split calibration and evaluation observations by time, plant, treatment or experiment where feasible.
Estimate parameters with uncertainty rather than reporting point estimates alone.
Check residual structure and whether errors depend systematically on light cycle, developmental stage or treatment.
Compare predictive likelihood, held-out RMSE/MAE or another declared metric across the baseline hierarchy.
Penalize the saturating model for extra parameters using a declared model-selection criterion.
observables: independently measured storage-input flux where available
mobilization or respiration flux where available
growth or remobilization response under changed light/source conditions
limiting_cases: Gamma=0 leaves only storage input and modeled release.
J_in=0 gives exponential depletion in the linear model.
K << K_half makes the saturating release approximately linear with rate J_max/K_half.
K >> K_half makes release approach J_max.
falsifiers: The model violates measured carbon/mass balance under the declared unit convention.
Parameters remain non-identifiable at the available measurement resolution and no independently measured flux resolves them.
Persistence or a simpler stock-flow baseline predicts held-out observations as well or better after complexity penalties.
The saturating release model does not materially improve out-of-sample performance over the linear model.
A claimed universal Starchforce interpretation is rejected if the result is fully explained by ordinary plant physiology and no preregistered residual mechanism remains.
null_result_interpretation: Failure of the benchmark is informative: it means this stock-flow form is not a useful description for the chosen biological system or measurement scale. It does not weaken or strengthen the project symbolism by itself.
maturity_boundary: This benchmark remains T2 because no real dataset is fitted in this record. T3 requires actual parameter constraints, uncertainty and evaluation results with dataset provenance.
